summary: Scientists and tech leaders, including executives at Microsoft and Google, issued a new warning that mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war. The statement, organized by the Center for AI Safety, was signed by hundreds of experts, including Sam Altman and Geoffrey Hinton. It comes amid growing concerns about advanced AI chatbots and regulatory efforts, with some critics arguing that such warnings hype AI capabilities and distract from immediate regulations.

claims.text: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.
claims.evidence_quote: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.

claims.text: The statement was posted on the Center for AI Safety's website and signed by hundreds of leading figures, including Sam Altman and Geoffrey Hinton.
claims.evidence_quote: Sam Altman, CEO of ChatGPT maker OpenAI, and Geoffrey Hinton, a computer scientist known as the godfather of artificial intelligence, were among the hundreds of leading figures who signed the statement, which was posted on the Center for AI Safety's website.

claims.text: The latest warning was intentionally succinct, just a single sentence, to encompass a broad coalition of scientists who might not agree on the most likely risks or the best solutions.
claims.evidence_quote: The latest warning was intentionally succinct — just a single sentence — to encompass a broad coalition of scientists who might not agree on the most likely risks or the best solutions to prevent them, said Dan Hendrycks, executive director of the San Francisco-based nonprofit Center for AI Safety, which organized the move.

claims.text: More than 1,000 researchers and technologists, including Elon Musk, had signed a much longer letter earlier this year calling for a six-month pause on AI development.
claims.evidence_quote: More than 1,000 researchers and technologists, including Elon Musk, had signed a much longer letter earlier this year calling for a six-month pause on AI development, saying it poses "profound risks to society and humanity."

claims.text: The latest statement was endorsed by Microsoft's chief technology and science officers, as well as Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google's AI research lab DeepMind, and two Google executives who lead its AI policy efforts.
claims.evidence_quote: By contrast, the latest statement was endorsed by Microsoft's chief technology and science officers, as well as Demis Hassabis, CEO of Google's AI research lab DeepMind, and two Google executives who lead its AI policy efforts.

claims.text: Some critics have complained that dire warnings about existential risks voiced by makers of AI have contributed to hyping up the capabilities of their products and distracting from calls for more immediate regulations.
claims.evidence_quote: Some critics have complained that dire warnings about existential risks voiced by makers of AI have contributed to hyping up the capabilities of their products and distracting from calls for more immediate regulations to rein in their real-world problems.

claims.text: Dan Hendrycks compared the situation to nuclear scientists in the 1930s warning people to be careful even though the bomb hadn't been developed yet.
claims.evidence_quote: He compared it to nuclear scientists in the 1930s warning people to be careful even though "we haven't quite developed the bomb yet."

claims.text: David Krueger, an assistant computer science professor at the University of Cambridge, said AI systems don't need to be self-aware or setting their own goals to pose a threat to humanity.
claims.evidence_quote: he said AI systems don't need to be self-aware or setting their own goals to pose a threat to humanity.

claims.text: Bill McKibben, who signed the letter, said given the failure to heed early warnings about climate change 35 years ago, it would be smart to think this through before it's all a done deal.
claims.evidence_quote: Given our failure to heed the early warnings about climate change 35 years ago, it feels to me as if it would be smart to actually think this one through before it's all a done deal.

claims.text: The European Union is expected to approve its AI Act later this year, which would be a pioneering regulation for AI.
claims.evidence_quote: It has sent countries around the world scrambling to come up with regulations for the developing technology, with the European Union blazing the trail with its AI Act expected to be approved later this year.
